ESTABLISHING STILL of Pyongyang, intro-card painted world, same film stock as the character cards: watercolor-and-oil, 2.5D architecture, quasi-sculpted giwa and stone, manga-adjacent ink line on the pavilion, NOT photoreal, NOT a 3D city render, NOT a Ghibli crowd catalog. FAR WIDE, slight dutch, dusk. ONE DEVICE: the red two-tier munru of the attached fortress board sitting on a grey stone ridge — KEEP this exact architecture (red pavilion, grey block wall, hongye). A tiny dark silhouette of a salt stall at the foot. Crushed dusk, one hard key from the west, long shadows. #C30000 as a thin red in the pavilion, never a glow. No cars. No modern city. No army. No text. PAINTED STILL — no faces and no recognisable person: the only figure is one anonymous dark silhouette, a shadow-shape against the light that belongs to the place; the place or object IS the subject. Sensual and suggestive by shape and motion alone, never anatomical, never explicit. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
